paragraphs: The services listed above take enquiries from people in Oldham, including the council's own Oldham Fostering Service, which recruits through Foster for Greater Manchester, a joint campaign of all ten councils in the city region. Oldham also runs the Mockingbird model, in which an experienced hub carer supports a small group of foster and kinship families; one Oldham group described in January 2025 linked eight families caring for 15 children.

The council has two schemes for children who need more than usual. Stepping Forward looks for full-time carers for children living in residential homes who do not need to be there; it is open to new and experienced carers, and suits people who have worked with young people, such as teachers, youth workers and residential staff. The council says it pays a combined fee and allowance of over £70,000 a year while the child is placed, with clinical psychology consultations, therapeutic support and help from the virtual school. One2One is therapeutic fostering for young people usually aged 6 to 18 whose earlier placements have broken down; carers need a spare room and to live in Oldham or within 20 miles, and couples must have lived together for a year or more.

Becoming a carer has six steps: an enquiry and information pack, a home visit, an application, checks and the Skills to Foster course (aimed to take about two months), a home study and the fostering panel (aimed to take about four months), and then a match with a child.
Speak to the council and two or three of the services above before choosing, and see the Rochdale, Manchester and Greater Manchester pages if you live near the borough's edge.
